title: Verbs with a fixed preposition: Páez and his network

sections.title: What you already know
sections.content: You know from B1 Unit 29 that many verbs need a fixed preposition (*acostumbrarse a*, *darse cuenta de*). Here you meet more of these verbs, the ones you need to describe a network of loyalty: who counted on whom, who depended on whom, who trusted whom.

sections.title: Verb + preposition
rows: Páez contaba con la lealtad de los llaneros.
Los jefes locales dependían de Páez.
Los llaneros confiaban en su jefe.

items.spanish: Páez contaba con la lealtad de los llaneros.
items.english: Páez counted on the loyalty of the llaneros.

items.spanish: Los jefes locales dependían de Páez.
items.english: The local chiefs depended on Páez.

items.spanish: Los hombres confiaban en el jefe.
Un caudillo no dependía de las leyes, dependía de las personas.
items.english: A caudillo did not depend on laws, he depended on people.

sections.content: The preposition belongs to the verb, and it does not change: *depender de*, *contar con*, *confiar en*. Before *el* it contracts: *dependía del jefe*. Do not use English as a guide: *depend on* is *depender de*, not *depender en*.
